Note::TexAccessor::nums¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::nums() const

Extract Unsigned Decimal Lexemes¶

nums() finds unsigned integer and decimal lexemes inside complete math fragments. 10 and 2.5 are tokens; a leading sign is a separate operator, so -3 contributes "-" through ops() and "3" through nums(). A scientific literal is not combined: 1e3 is read according to the lexical grammar rather than converted to a numeric value.

The method is an extractor, not a parser or cast. Returned values remain Text, preserve their authored spelling, and are never range-checked or rounded. Prose numbers, escaped dollar amounts, and unmatched math delimiters are ignored. Every complete $, $$, \(, and \[ region is scanned in source order.

Variable counts are represented by flat tokens plus one cumulative offset per receiver cell. Empty lanes therefore remain visible without fabricated values. Undefined input propagates and non-text input throws. The scan is linear.

Example 1: Exclude Prose And Preserve Spelling¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(prose 99; $x_1 + \sin(\alpha) = 2.5$)",
        R"(\[\beta \leq y^2\] and \(\sqrt{z}\))",
        R"(escaped \$7 and plain theta)",
        R"($$\argmax_x f(x) \approx 10$$)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().nums();
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["2.5", "2", "10"]

99 and 7 are outside valid math regions.

Example 2: Offsets For A Rank-Two Receiver¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (auto value : offsets) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

0 1 2 2 3

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().nums().tokens().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().nums();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "numbers Int64: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

false
numbers Int64: rejected
